description:
PearCal is a peer-to-peer calendar app that syncs directly between devices — no server, no cloud, no accounts required.

Your calendar data never leaves your group. It lives only on the devices of the people you choose to share with, powered by Hypercore Protocol.

FEATURES

Peer Groups

Create a group and invite others via a share link or QR code. Each group has its own color and avatar. Members see only the events shared with them.

Events & Reminders

Create one-time or recurring events. Set a reminder time per event. Selectively share events with specific group members — not everyone in a group has to see every event.

Holidays
Optional US, Canada, and UK public holiday calendars. Toggle per country from your profile. Holiday events are read-only and stored locally only.

Privacy First

No account creation. No email address. No tracking. No ads. Your data stays on your devices.

Open Source
PearCal is free and open source. Source code is available on GitHub.

PERMISSIONS

Camera — used to set your profile photo and scan QR invite codes.
Photo Library — used to set your profile photo.
whatsNew:
## What's Changed

New Features

- Import and export calendars on the computer app. You can bring a .ics file
into PearCal Desktop, and save your own events back out as one.
- Choose where imported events go. When you import a calendar file, PearCal now
asks once whether those events should stay private to you or join one of your
shared calendars, instead of deciding for you. It tells you who will be able
to see them before you confirm.
- See what is using your disk space. Settings on the computer app has a new
Storage section showing what PearCal is keeping and how much of it is old
history you no longer need.

Improvements

- The always-on helper on a Mac keeps running after you log out, so your
calendar carries on syncing when nobody is signed in.

Bug Fixes

- Installing the always-on helper on a server with no desktop no longer ends
with an error message. The install had actually worked; only the report was
wrong.
- Fixed a Mac problem where two copies of the helper could end up fighting each
other, and another that could leave it switched off without saying so.
